$comment: The most each public page may ship on its first load, in bytes, compressed (gzip for text; fonts as served), by kind and in total. scripts/check-performance-budget.mjs measures the built output against it on every pull request (Checks, 'Public site checks'), from the files a page's own HTML names, not from a timed run, and fails naming the page and the kind. scripts/performance-budget.mjs says what counts as first load. Scripts, styles, fonts and data were set on 2026-11-23 from what the build then shipped (after the front page became the list of starter canvases), plus 5%, rounded up to 100 bytes: a budget holds a page where it is, it does not say the page is light enough (lane A makes the heavy ones lighter, and lowers the limits as it does). A page's own HTML has one ceiling for every page, 30,000 bytes: the words on a page are not what makes it slow, and a limit of a few bytes over today's text would fail every time a sentence is added. The total is the sum of the kinds. To raise a limit, say why in the pull request. node scripts/check-performance-budget.mjs --propose prints the numbers for the build in front of it.
